Wonderful Cavatelli and Rustic Italian Flavors
Oct 2026 • Couples
We had an 8 p.m. dinner at Macchialina Taverna Rustica during our visit to Miami Beach. We were seated toward the far end of the outdoor alley dining area. It was so dark that I couldn't read the menu. I had to take several pictures of it with my phone just to figure out what to order. My husband could read his menu because light from a wall sconce shone on his side of the table. I wished there had been a light on our table, but I looked around and didn't see any on the other tables either.

We shared an Insalata Tricolore salad, and of course I had to try the Gnocco Fritto, the puffed fried bread from Emilia-Romagna. The order came with three pieces. It wasn't as oily as roti or funnel cake, but it was satisfyingly carby!

Our favorite dish was the Cavatelli Macchialina. I loved the rich, robust flavor of the sauce, which had a wonderful complexity and marriage of flavors. I thought it was even better than some of the pasta sauces we'd enjoyed in Rome, Italy. My only complaint was the spiciness, which was a bit much for me. The menu described baby meatballs, but I counted only two in my portion, while my husband had four. The cavatelli pasta itself was perfect!

My husband ordered the tiramisu for dessert, but it wasn't what we expected. Rather than the creamy dessert we normally associate with tiramisu, it reminded us more of shaved ice with a hint of coffee flavor. We missed the creaminess, but it was refreshing and something different for the Miami heat. We shared a Limoncello, which was a popular drink that night. 

Overall, I really enjoyed our dinner at Macchialina, especially the Cavatelli Macchialina with its wonderfully rich, flavorful sauce. The Gnocco Fritto was a fun, new treat, too. Despite a few things I would have preferred differently, I'm glad we dined here and had the opportunity to try their take on rustic Italian cooking.

Not so Italian, but it works
Apr 2024 • Family
The experience at Macchialina Taverna Rustica was a mix of emotions. On the one hand, it is undeniable that the place is a success, since even on a Monday night it was packed with people. However, there are some aspects that could be significantly improved.

The main problem was the noise level, which made conversation and the overall experience difficult. Also, the prices were quite high, averaging around $120 per person, which is a bit steep for what the place offers.

Although it is advertised as an Italian restaurant, the American influence is evident in everything from the decor to the food itself. Unfortunately, this fusion does not always work in your favor, as you miss out on some essential characteristics of authentic Italian cuisine. For example, there was no olive oil, no bread, no Parmesan cheese to accompany the pasta on the tables, and there were not even tablecloths, which is in line with the rustic style of the place, but may be disappointing for those looking for a more rustic experience. refined.

As for the food, the flavors were normal, without particularly standing out. Nothing out of the ordinary was experienced in terms of taste or presentation, which was a bit disappointing considering the price.

In short, Macchialina Taverna Rustica seems to have found the right balance between American and Italian, which may be a major factor in its success. However, for those looking for a more authentic experience of Italian cuisine, this may not be the ideal place.
